blocks.content: Because DNH&DD spans two very different micro-regions — the hilly, forested inland tract of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and the flat coastal enclaves of Daman and Diu — its geography chapter effectively covers two distinct ecological zones under one UT. Exam questions often test this inland-vs-coastal contrast directly.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India extends between latitudes 8°4'N and 37°6'N and longitudes 68°7'E and 97°25'E in the Northern and Eastern hemispheres.
The climate of India is predominantly driven by the tropical monsoon system, influenced by southwest summer monsoons and northeast winter monsoons.
Tropical Deciduous Forests are the most widespread vegetation cover across the Indian subcontinent.
The Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N) divides India into almost equal tropical and sub-tropical climate zones.

blocks.content: Dadra & Nagar Haveli lies close to the Western Ghats' northern extension (the Sahyadri hill ranges), giving it a hilly, forested character especially in its north-eastern and eastern parts, with elevations rising towards these outlying Sahyadri spurs.

Daman and Diu, by contrast, are low-lying coastal enclaves directly on the Arabian Sea, with sandy beaches, tidal creeks, and flat coastal plains typical of Gujarat's Saurashtra and south Gujarat coastline.

The Daman Ganga River is the most important river of the UT, flowing from the Western Ghats through Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman before draining into the Arabian Sea at Daman — it and its tributaries (including the Piparia, Sakartod and Kharkhadi streams) are central to the territory's irrigation and drinking-water supply.

The Madhuban Dam, built across the Daman Ganga near Silvassa, is the principal water-storage and irrigation infrastructure of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and a well-known local landmark and picnic/tourism spot.
Tropical Deciduous Forests form the most widespread vegetation cover in India.

cells: ≈ 603 sq km (Dadra & Nagar Haveli ≈ 491 sq km; Daman ≈ 72 sq km; Diu ≈ 40 sq km)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Only Dadra & Nagar Haveli borders Maharashtra — Daman and Diu are both entirely surrounded by Gujarat alone. This is a frequently confused point since people assume the whole UT borders both states equally.

The UT has a broadly tropical climate but with a distinct micro-variation: Dadra & Nagar Haveli, being inland and hillier, experiences a somewhat more extreme tropical climate with hotter summers and heavier monsoon rainfall (owing to its proximity to the Western Ghats' orographic rain belt), while Daman and Diu enjoy a milder, more equable maritime climate typical of coastal Gujarat.

Western Ghats, Andaman & Nicobar, North-East Hills

cells: Hot and humid; Dadra & Nagar Haveli sees higher daytime temperatures than the coast
South-West monsoon brings heavy rainfall, especially in the hillier Nagar Haveli tract (orographic effect from the Western Ghats)
Mild and pleasant on the coast (Daman, Diu); slightly cooler nights inland at Dadra & Nagar Haveli

blocks.content: Dadra & Nagar Haveli has a comparatively high proportion of forest cover for such a small territory, dominated by dry deciduous and moist deciduous forest types typical of the northern Western Ghats foothills — teak (Sagwan), khair, and mixed deciduous species are prominent, supporting the territory's tribal-dominated economy through minor forest produce (timber, bamboo, mahua, tendu leaves).

Daman and Diu, being coastal and largely urbanised/agricultural, have far more limited natural forest cover; their vegetation instead includes coastal scrub, casuarina and coconut/palm plantations along the shoreline, and mangrove patches in sheltered creeks and estuaries.

The Aviary at Jampore (Daman) and various eco-parks and coastal green belts have been developed in recent years as part of the UT's environmental and tourism initiatives, alongside afforestation drives in Dadra & Nagar Haveli's hilly tracts.

items: Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 Indian States: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, and Mizoram.
Retreating monsoons during October-November bring maximum rainfall to the Coromandel coast (Tamil Nadu).
Sundarbans in West Bengal represent the world's largest contiguous mangrove forest ecosystem.

cells: Dry & moist deciduous forest — teak, khair, mixed deciduous species; significant forest cover relative to UT size
Coastal scrub, casuarina avenues, coconut/palm plantations, patchy mangroves in creeks
Sparse coastal scrub and grassland; limited tree cover owing to salinity and wind exposure; some casuarina plantations

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Vegetation contrast to remember: Dadra & Nagar Haveli = deciduous forest / tribal forest-produce economy; Daman & Diu = coastal scrub, palms, and mangrove patches — this inland-vs-coastal split mirrors the terrain contrast and is a natural pairing for MCQs.

Main river: Daman Ganga, dammed at Madhuban Dam near Silvassa.
Only Dadra & Nagar Haveli borders Maharashtra; all three enclaves border Gujarat.
Dadra & Nagar Haveli: hilly, forested (Western Ghats/Sahyadri spurs), dry/moist deciduous forest, teak-dominant.
Daman & Diu: flat coastal plain, casuarina/palm vegetation, patchy mangroves; Diu is an island with sparse cover.
